Class WireTime

java.lang.Object
de.hallerweb.enterprise.prioritize.dto.WireTime
public final class WireTime extends Object
Converts between the entities' server-zone LocalDateTime and the Instant the REST API puts on the wire.

Why this exists: OpenAPI's format: date-time is RFC 3339, which requires a UTC offset. Jackson serializes a LocalDateTime without one ("2026-08-02T21:40:20.81039"), so every generated, statically typed client — which maps date-time to OffsetDateTime — failed to parse those fields, while the Instant-backed fields on the same API parsed fine. Mapping to Instant at the DTO boundary makes the emitted JSON match the published contract. Entities keep their LocalDateTime columns; nothing about persistence changes.

Zone: every LocalDateTime in the model is server-zone wall clock — it originates from LocalDateTime.now(), and TaskSchedule.nextFireAt is explicitly normalized to the server zone by TaskScheduleService. ZoneId.systemDefault() is therefore the correct — and only correct — interpretation of the stored values.

Author:
peter haller
